Certainly! Here are two hints for the given step:

**Hint 1:** Consider the properties of mean-centering in linear regression. When you mean-center the design matrix $\mathbb{X}$ to obtain $\dot{\mathbb{X}}$, the intercept term (first column) remains unchanged, while the other columns are adjusted to have a mean of zero. How does this affect the coefficients of the linear model?

**Hint 2:** Think about the relationship between the coefficients obtained from the original design matrix $\mathbb{X}$ and the mean-centered design matrix $\dot{\mathbb{X}}$. Specifically, focus on how mean-centering impacts the estimation of the slope coefficients, particularly $\hat{ eta}_1$ and $\hat{\gamma}_1$.
